clue.text: Queen's husband longs for a republic

parts.note: Prince Philip was the husband of Queen Elizabeth II
to long for something is to pine for it

explanation.surface: The royal consort is pining for life in a country without a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Philippines is an island nation in south-east Asia governed as a republic.

clue.text: One old car in a pile-up

explanation.surface: A battered vehicle caught up in a motorway crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A clapped-out motor is slangily called a heap, and a jumbled mass of things is also a heap.

clue.text: The song told a story

explanation.surface: A singer whose ballad recounted a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The song' points to the German art song, a Lied; 'told a story' means fibbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lied is a German art song, and someone who told a story in the sense of a fib was untruthful.

clue.text: Brave child backed by his mother

definitions.text: Brave child backed by his mother

parts.words: Brave child backed by his mother
parts.note: a Native American warrior is called a brave; his infant is carried on the mother's back, so 'backed' is literal

explanation.surface: A courageous youngster supported by a loving parent.
explanation.definitionFit: A Native American baby carried in a pouch on its mother's back has this name.

clue.text: May now be written like this!

definitions.text: May now be written like this!

parts.words: May now be written like this!
parts.note: in May, a letter referring to the current month uses an abbreviation of Latin ...

explanation.surface: Advice on how a modern author might express permission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the verb of permission but is the month; in old business letters 'the 5th inst.' meant the 5th of this month.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation of instant, meaning of the present month, is how a date in the current month like May is written.

clue.text: Noise or disturbance can be wearing

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Constant racket or upheaval can be tiring to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbance' rearranges NOISE and OR; 'wearing' looks like 'tiring' but means wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is the gradual wearing away of rock or soil.

clue.text: Withhold payment for use of the port

definitions.text: Withhold payment for use of the port

parts.words: Withhold payment for use of the port
parts.note: read as harbour (keep hold of) plus dues (payment), it names charges for using a port

explanation.surface: Refuse to pay the fee for docking.
explanation.definitionFit: Charges levied on ships for using a harbour's facilities go by this name.

clue.text: Second print out is lacking in character

indicators.note: out here means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A second printing that turns out dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of SECOND and PRINT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dull and featureless, with no distinctive qualities, is called nondescript.

clue.text: Card game depending on luck for a change

indicators.note: for a change signals the letters of the preceding words being reshuffled

explanation.surface: A gambling game that relies on chance, for once.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is an old gambling card game in which players bet on the order of cards drawn.

clue.text: Weapon used to liquidate people

parts.note: liquidate usually means kill, but read literally it means to make people wet with liquid

explanation.surface: A gun for assassinations.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy gun that squirts liquid is a playful weapon for soaking people.

clue.text: Jack and Edward retired

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB (able seaman)
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Two men named Jack and Edward have stopped working.
explanation.definitionFit: Retired here means gone to bed for the night, so the person is in bed.

clue.text: Looking for a short cut for riders to use

parts.note: hunting for something is looking for it
to crop is to cut short, as in a crop of hair

explanation.surface: Searching for a quicker route for horsemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a short cut' looks like a quicker path, but it is a crop, a close-cut hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: A short riding whip with a loop is carried by horse riders.

clue.text: Confined to one game-but good at others?

definitions.text: Confined to one game-but good at others?

parts.words: Confined to one game-but good at others?
parts.note: cricketers good at batting and bowling are said to be versatile; the question mark marks the playful reading

explanation.surface: A player tied to one sport who might shine in others.
explanation.walkthrough: The term is used in cricket for players skilled at both batting and bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: Versatile people competent in many fields, especially sportspeople with several skills, have this name.

clue.text: Liberate one soul in torment

indicators.note: something in torment is twisted and racked, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Free a single tortured spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: To unloose is to set free or release from bonds.

clue.text: Spritely number in fine disarray

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other here
disarray means disorder, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A tune in a jumbled state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disarray' rearranges FINE to EFIN, and 'in' places L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Spritely here means like a sprite, small and fairy-like, which is what elfin means.

clue.text: Flags show we've won a mountain pass

parts.note: col is a word for a pass between mountains
after a victory a team says it's ours

explanation.surface: A team raises its banners in triumph on a mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's or ship's colours are its flags.

clue.text: Numbers of Romans about the city

explanation.surface: Roman population figures concerning a town.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition reads the letters as Roman numerals: C, IV, I, C.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is spelt entirely in Roman numerals, and civic means relating to a city or town.

clue.text: Sort of marbles Nigel played with

indicators.note: fiddling with something rearranges it, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A boy named Nigel playing a game of marbles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'played with' rearranges NIGEL; the marbles are statues from the Parthenon, not toys.
explanation.definitionFit: The Parthenon sculptures in the British Museum are known after Lord Elgin, who removed them.

clue.text: Right-minded man's essay about love

indicators.note: about signals one piece going around another

parts.note: to essay is to try
love is zero in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: A virtuous person's composition on the subject of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right-minded' means right-wing; the essay is an attempt, TRY, not a composition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Conservative is politically on the right, hence a right-minded man.

clue.text: Duck on the German river

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, shown as O
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: A duck swimming on a river in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a river in central Europe forming part of the German-Polish border.

clue.text: Operatic heroine many imitate

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, hence many

explanation.surface: Lots of people copy a famous opera character.
explanation.definitionFit: To mimic is to copy someone's manner or voice.

clue.text: Rainy day in the near future?

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the wet season it describes

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday
soon means before long

explanation.surface: A wet day forecast for shortly.
explanation.definitionFit: The monsoon is the seasonal wind of South Asia that brings heavy rain.

clue.text: Conditions that might affect mail etc.

indicators.note: to affect something is to alter it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Weather that could delay the post and other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that might affect' rearranges MAIL and ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: Climate is the prevailing weather pattern of a region.

clue.text: Turn one out, though it's free of charge

indicators.note: out here means put into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Kick someone out, even though there's no fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges TURNONE; 'free of charge' looks like costless but means electrically neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic particle with no electric charge sits in the atomic nucleus.

clue.text: Big shot in the film world

definitions.text: Big shot in the film world

parts.words: Big shot in the film world
parts.note: a big shot is a VIP, but read literally it is a camera shot filling the frame

explanation.surface: An important person in the movie industry.
explanation.definitionFit: A film shot taken at short range shows the subject large on screen.

clue.text: One hundred lines for conduct

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
an ode is a poem, a set of lines

explanation.surface: A school punishment of writing out lines for bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: A code is a set of rules governing behaviour, as in a code of conduct.

clue.text: Passage for one from Oslo

indicators.note: coming from the given letters, rearranged, signals an anagram here

explanation.surface: A single ticket out of Norway's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges OSLO; 'Passage' is a piece of music, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical passage performed by a single player is a solo.

clue.text: Foreign money for rail development

indicators.note: a development changes the form of something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Overseas investment funding a railway project.
explanation.definitionFit: The lira was the currency of Italy and is still that of Turkey.

clue.text: It's bent on submission

parts.note: bent on looks like intent upon, but read literally a joint is bent when ... in submission

explanation.surface: Someone determined to give in.
explanation.definitionFit: Kneeling to show deference means bending the leg joint between thigh and shin.

clue.text: Man uses mashie and spoon going round

indicators.note: something going round is turned about, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A golfer uses old clubs during a round.
explanation.walkthrough: A mashie and a spoon are old names for golf clubs; 'going round' rearranges their letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Homo sapiens is the scientific name of the human species, mankind.

clue.text: They move a boat across water or round a point

definitions.text: They move a boat across water

indicators.note: round signals one piece placed around another

parts.note: taken as written
S is south, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Rowing a boat over a lake or around a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts OR around A, giving OAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowers propel a boat with long poles with flat blades.

clue.text: Exact monies may be required to pay them

definitions.text: Exact monies may be required to pay them

indicators.note: required here plays on re-quired, meaning reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Precise sums of cash must be handed over to settle these.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be required' rearranges EXACT and MONIES; the whole clue also defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Levies on earnings demand exact sums of money from taxpayers.
